Then, over-correcting, a concept search reported the three-axis method and the authorship lesson as ALREADY PRESENT — 'cardinality' had hit a rule about ROWSKIPS rejection and 'authorship' had hit feedback_only_modify_our_own_code. Both were false positives and both would have left real knowledge in the chat. One failure mode says 'not there' when it is; the other says 'there' when it is not, and the second is worse because it ends the search.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts traceability above velocity. A rule nobody can execute produces the APPEARANCE of a control while the loss keeps happening silently, which is the irreversible failure it warns against — the loss is invisible precisely because a rule exists.
rules.evidence: scripts/verify_generated.py first run found budget_rate_graph.json drifted; rule #180 existed and was violated 4x in s098; dedup failed 2x
rules.how_to_apply: When about to write a feedback rule, ask first: could a script detect this violation? If yes, write the script and let the rule point at it. The rules store is for JUDGEMENT — what to measure, what to distrust, when to stop. Mechanical invariants belong in scripts/verify_generated.py, brain_v2/promote.py, brain_v2/verify_claims.py and their siblings, and the close should RUN them rather than recite them.
rules.rule: A rule that can only be obeyed by REMEMBERING it will be broken, including by the agent that wrote it. For any failure that is MECHANICAL — a substitution that must land, an output that must match its generator, a store that must be searched before writing — do not add a rule. Add a CHECK that runs and fails loudly. If the check cannot be written, say so explicitly instead of writing a rule that will read as coverage and provide none.
rules.why: s098, and the evidence is against myself. Rule #180 — 'a silent replace is a silent defect' — ALREADY EXISTED and I broke it FOUR times in this one session: each time a template replace missed its anchor, the script printed OK because the Python still parsed, and the page shipped with a raw token or a stray %s. Every one was caught afterwards, by hand, one at a time. Three companions carried the line 'never edit the HTML, edit the builder' and nothing verified it — when a check was finally written, its FIRST run found budget_rate_graph.json already out of step with its generator, and nobody had known. The dedup discipline failed twice more, in mirror-image forms. Four documented rule-violations by the author of the rules is not a discipline problem; it is proof that rules do not work on mechanical failures.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 values traceability: an exclusion with its reason recorded is traceable, while a check quietly ignored by its reader loses the signal AND the record that a decision was ever made.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/stop_integrity_hook.py NOT_ALGORITHMS; verified quiet on the ten and firing on a new file
rules.how_to_apply: Give the check an explicit exclusion set IN THE CODE, with a comment saying when it was triaged and on what basis — never a silent filter. Then verify BOTH directions: that it goes quiet on the reviewed set, and that it still fires on a newly introduced case. The second test is the one that proves the exclusion did not just switch the check off.
rules.rule: Any automated check that reports CANDIDATES rather than certainties must be able to record 'reviewed and deliberately excluded', with the reason written beside it. Without that, it repeats the same finding every run, the reader learns to skip it, and the control silently becomes decoration — while still appearing to be a control, which is worse than having none. A gate with no memory of its own decisions can only repeat itself.
rules.why: s098, on the first real use of stop_integrity_hook.py. It flagged ten process_mining scripts as absent from the algorithm arsenal. Triaged one by one, EIGHT are helpers or pipeline steps of 54-135 lines, two are analyses, none declares itself an algorithm and none is reusable on another installation — which is the bar. The honest verdict was that NONE should be registered. But that verdict had nowhere to live, so the gate would have reported the same ten every session forever. The degradation the hook was explicitly designed to avoid reappeared through the back door, one commit after the design note warning about it.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts traceability above velocity and calls losing it irreversible. Losing the memory of WHY a decision was made is the purest form of that loss, and it is the asset with the least protection precisely because it is the smallest.
rules.evidence: knowledge/recovery_runbook.md; drill 595 files in / 595 out / 474 memory, OK; scripts/backup_golden.py aborts below 50 memory files
rules.how_to_apply: Follow the universal standard at ecosystem-coordinator/.knowledge/way-of-working/project-durability-and-recovery.md. Reference implementation: scripts/backup_golden.py (both assets, one --dest) and knowledge/recovery_runbook.md. Rehearse with `--restore <pkg> --to <tmp>` and paste the ACTUAL output into the runbook — the last real drill, not the expected one. And bound the worst case for reconstructible assets with a manifest of what was loaded and under which rules; without it recovery is archaeology, with it it is a script.
rules.rule: A backup that has never been RESTORED is a hypothesis. Every backup this project writes must ship with a rehearsed restore, and the recovery runbook must live in the REPO so it can be read from origin when the machine it describes is gone. Six rules: MEASURE before designing (the irreplaceable asset is rarely the big one); EXCLUDE with the reason written down; VERIFY the exclusion by reading the written package, not by trusting the filter; REFUSE to write an empty backup; RESTORE to a staging directory, never over the live target; and state explicitly what is NOT recoverable.
rules.why: s098. Every session close for months had RESTATED that the Golden DB and ~/.claude are local-only and git does not protect them. When it was finally checked there were ZERO copies of either and no script to make one — stating a risk is not managing it, and a reminder that repeats and is never executed is the APPEARANCE of a control, which is worse than none because nobody looks again. The same session also had 73 unpushed commits: git protects nothing you have not pushed. And measuring inverted the intuition — 1,836 MB of transcripts and 16.33 GB of database are both reconstructible, while the 1.5 MB of memory is the only thing nothing can rebuild. Then TESTING the backup found it captured 4 files and zero memory (pathlib resolves `dir/**` as directories, not recursive files) AND wrote the package anyway.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands precision anchored in evidence. Naming the kind of work before doing it is the first precision available; skipping it makes every later step approximate.
rules.evidence: .claude/skills/sap_incident_analyst/SKILL.md Step 0; INC-000006313 + INC-000011781 vs INC-000005240
rules.how_to_apply: Step 0 of .claude/skills/sap_incident_analyst/SKILL.md. State the track explicitly in your first response on the ticket, and say why. If you find yourself writing 'how it should work' for a request that is just 'add this person', you triaged wrong. Both tracks still share: BRAIN LOOKUP, provisional-until-confirmed, the user gate, and rebuild-only-at-the-end.
rules.rule: Triage every support item into one of TWO tracks BEFORE any lookup or analysis. TRACK A = DIAGNOSIS: the unknown is why the system behaved this way; the output is a root cause. TRACK B = OPERATIONAL ACTION: what to do is already known and executing it correctly is the work; the output is an executed, verified change plus the reusable procedure. Tell them apart in one read: an action verb aimed at a named person/entity from someone with the authority to ask for it is B; a symptom, an error number, a 'this fails' is A. Ambiguous items default to A unless there is an authorizing document, in which case they are B.
rules.why: s099. The skill had one protocol shaped entirely around diagnosis, so the operational changes (INC-000006313, INC-000011781) were pushed through a root-cause workflow that asks the wrong questions. Track B's risks are not Track A's: A fails by chasing the wrong mechanism (INC-000005240 burned 154K tokens on FMDERIVE), B fails by executing the requester's summary instead of the authority and by never looking at the population around the change. One protocol for both means one set of blind spots applied to work that does not share them.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 requires verifiable evidence behind every action. A forwarded sentence is not evidence of what was authorized; the signed letter is.
rules.evidence: knowledge/incidents/INC-000011781_ubo_bcm_add_ritter.md §1-§4; INC-000006313 BEGDA gap
rules.how_to_apply: Track B step B1. Record the authority reference, its date, its effective date, and the complete operation list. Use the authority's effective date as BEGDA, not the execution date — INC-000006313 used the execution date and opened a 7-day audit gap for nothing.
rules.rule: On any operational change, the authorizing DOCUMENT is the specification — never the requester's summary. Read the TRS letter, the bank carton, the signed approval, and execute the full set of operations it mandates, including the ones nobody mentioned. No authority document = no change spec; stop and ask.
rules.why: INC-000011781. The request said 'can you please add Renata RITTER for UBO in BCM'. The two authoritative TRS letters (FIN.8/MOD/10.0000003618 and ...3617, both 24/03/2026) said ADD Ritter AND DELETE Von Michael MARTIN. Executing the note would have added the new signatory and left an unauthorized one active on two bank accounts. A requester's note is a pointer to the change, not the change.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts knowledge above velocity. Closing the ticket at the row you changed is the fast path; sweeping the population is where the ticket turns into knowledge that outlives it.
rules.evidence: knowledge/incidents/INC-000011781_ubo_bcm_add_ritter.md §0; Zagentexecution/quality_checks/bcm_*.py
rules.how_to_apply: Track B step B8. Diff the system population against the authority document, both directions (present-but-unauthorized AND authorized-but-missing). Promote the diff to a script. The BCM family is the worked pattern: bcm_signatory_reconciliation_check.py, bcm_role_gap_check.py, bcm_release_vs_approve.py.
rules.rule: After executing an operational change, reconcile the ENTIRE population against the authority — not just the row you touched. Whatever the sweep finds becomes a recurring check under Zagentexecution/quality_checks/. This is Track B's equivalent of Track A's class generalization: one ticket, one standing control.
rules.why: INC-000011781. Nobody asked us to audit the UBO panel; the ask was to add one person. The sweep against the carton found De Sousa Carvalho 10016038 active on all 4 nodes with full signing rights and BCM_REV_REJ_PAY since Jan-2024 while absent from the carton — roughly 18 months of over-authorization that no standing control was looking for. The ticket was not the finding; the ticket was the occasion to look.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001: velocity that leaves no trace is the expensive kind. A procedure written on the 2nd occurrence is traceability that pays compound interest.
rules.evidence: INC-000006313 -> INC-000011781; knowledge/domains/Treasury/bcm_signatory_change_solution_design.md
rules.how_to_apply: Track B step B9. Before closing, ask: how many times have we done this scenario? Look it up via the incident records' `scenario` field. If the answer is >=2 and there is no procedure doc, writing it is part of the ticket, not a nice-to-have.
rules.rule: Track the occurrence count of every operational scenario. 1st occurrence leaves an incident doc + a first-class record + the rules doc that explains target selection. 2nd occurrence MUST leave a procedure doc + a recurring check + a companion, so the 3rd is mechanical. From the 3rd on, execute from the procedure; if you had to re-derive anything, the procedure was incomplete and fixing it is part of that ticket.
rules.why: s099. This is how the ecosystem gets cheaper instead of merely busier. The BCM signatory pattern proves it: the 2nd execution (INC-000011781) was faster than the 1st (INC-000006313) AND caught drift the 1st never looked for, because the 1st had left behind bcm_signatory_rules.md and a reconciliation check. Without that promotion step, each ticket re-derives the same mechanism and the cost per ticket stays flat forever.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 calls lost traceability irreversible. Knowledge that exists but cannot be reached by the traversal the protocol mandates is, operationally, lost.
rules.evidence: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/incident_record_coverage_check.py; incidents.json 7 -> 10 records s099
rules.how_to_apply: Write the record in the SAME action as the doc, never 'later'. Before closing any support work run the check (exit 0 = clean) and then rebuild. If you only have time for one of the two artifacts, write the record — a record without prose is still findable; prose without a record is not.
rules.rule: An incident is not captured until it has a first-class record in brain_v2/incidents/incidents.json. A markdown file under knowledge/incidents/ is prose on disk: BRAIN LOOKUP traverses brain_state.incidents -> indexes.by_incident -> objects[X], and a doc with no record is in none of those. Gate it with Zagentexecution/quality_checks/incident_record_coverage_check.py.
rules.why: s099 opened and found 11 docs on disk against 7 records. Three incidents were invisible: INC-000011781 (the richest BCM signatory precedent we have — IT1218 node selection, the drift sweep, the role gap), INC-180995 and INC-CLASS-LOSS-2026-06. The PMO had recorded 'TODO: run rebuild_all.py to fold INC-000011781 in' on 2026-06-18 and it never ran. A TODO is not a control; the next agent on a sibling BCM ticket would have started from zero.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands verifiable evidence. An empty result set is only evidence once the method is shown capable of producing a non-empty one.
rules.evidence: Zagentexecution/mcp-backend-server-python/YRGGBS00_SOURCE.txt:1547 FORM u917 vs claim 116 layer (4); claim 484 supersedes 116
rules.how_to_apply: Positive control first: grep for something you KNOW is in the file (its own FORM names, 'ENDFORM') and confirm you get hits. If that returns 0, your pipeline is broken, not the system. Use `python brain_v2/graph_queries.py code <obj>` to get the encoding-normalised primary source and the STUB_AT_CANONICAL flag before grepping, and `graph_queries.py section <routine>` / `blocking_code` instead of raw text search for behaviour. State the negative as 'not found by <method>', never as 'does not exist'.
rules.rule: A search that returns nothing is evidence about the SEARCH, not about the system. Before concluding 'X does not exist', prove the search could have found X: check the file ENCODING (UTF-16 returns 0 for every ASCII pattern), the CASE (ABAP source is conventionally lowercase; SAP field names are quoted uppercase in docs), and whether you searched the FULL body or a stub. Then check the ABSTRACTION: a table-level search cannot see logic that lives behind an exit call — GB931 holds CHECKID '=U917', never the field the FORM reads.
rules.why: s099. Claim 116 was published TIER_1 saying the PPC capture control did not exist, on the strength of 'zero matches for LZBKZ in YRGGBS00's 1,592-line source'. The file is UTF-16 and the ABAP is lowercase; FORM u917 sits at line 1547 and blocks the posting. Three silent failures stacked — wrong encoding, wrong case, and a corpus copy that was a 29-line stub. On that claim a KU was opened proposing four ways to BUILD a control that already existed, waiting on a decision from two named people. A zero-result search feels like evidence of absence and is the cheapest way to publish a confident lie.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands exact numbers with checkable provenance. An amount without its unit is not a number, and a sum across units is not a measurement.
rules.evidence: claims 492 -> 493; REGUH RWBTR/WAERS for the 58 EG Citi-routed lines
rules.how_to_apply: Any SELECT that sums an amount must carry its currency field in the GROUP BY, or the query is wrong. When comparing entities, prefer COUNTS or shares — they are currency-free. State the currency of every figure you report, and if it is a mix, say 'mixed currencies, not summable'.
rules.rule: Never SUM a document amount without grouping by its currency, and never label the result with a currency you did not convert into. REGUH-RWBTR, BSEG-DMBTR/WRBTR, FPAYP-* are all in the document or payment currency. If a total must span currencies, either group by WAERS and report the vector, or convert explicitly and say so.
rules.why: s099. I reported Egypt's Citi exposure as 'USD 3,285,100' from SUM(RWBTR) over rows that were mostly EGP. The largest entries were 360,600 and 200,000 EGP — about USD 7,200 and USD 4,000. That single number turned a routine country configuration into what I presented as an order-of-magnitude outlier, and it drove a wrong recommendation until JP challenged it. A cross-currency sum is not merely imprecise; it manufactures a finding that does not exist.

rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands that a claim (here, a script's PASS verdict) be anchored in checkable evidence. A PASS that includes an untested dimension is precision theater: it reads as measured and is actually approximated by omission.
rules.evidence: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/ppc_country_consistency_check.py (fixed s099, exit 3 path added); prior text: 'PASS - every configured country has ... and no degenerate usage' printed while check D was skipped for lack of REGUP in the Gold DB
rules.how_to_apply: Any script with more than one independent sub-check must track which sub-checks actually executed. If any did not, the closing message must name it explicitly as SKIPPED (never silently merged into the aggregate verdict) and the script should return a THIRD exit code (not 0=clean, not 1=finding) so a caller cannot mistake 'ran clean' for 'ran completely'. See the fix applied the same session: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/ppc_country_consistency_check.py now returns 3 when any check is skipped, with the skipped list printed even inside an otherwise-PASS run.
rules.rule: When one sub-check inside a multi-check script cannot run (a precondition is missing — a table absent from the Gold DB, a source unreachable, an input undefined), the script must report that sub-check as SKIPPED, with a distinct signal (message + a different exit code from clean-pass), and must NEVER fold its absence into an overall PASS message that names the untested condition as satisfied.
rules.why: s099. Zagentexecution/quality_checks/ppc_country_consistency_check.py's check D (degenerate usage) needs REGUP, which is not in the Gold DB. The first version printed a NOTE that check D was skipped, then — because no other check produced a finding — printed 'PASS ... and no degenerate usage' and exited 0. That sentence asserts the one thing that was never measured. This is adjacent to rule #180 (a silent replace is a silent defect) but the mechanism is different: #180 is a WRITE that silently no-ops while the script still reports success; this is a READ that silently cannot execute while the script's SUMMARY still claims full coverage. Both are 'green paint over an unknown', but the fix lives in different code (a text-replace guard vs a coverage-aware exit path), so this is its own rule, not a duplicate.

rules.how_to_apply:
1. Before closing, run the fresh-session probe instead of asserting coverage: grep BRAIN_INDEX.md and MEMORY.md for the session's key terms. Zero hits means the work is invisible however well stored.
2. Fix at the GENERATOR (brain_v2/build_brain_index.py), never by hand-editing the generated index - it is rewritten on every rebuild and a hand edit is lost.
3. Prefer a fix that covers the NEXT case, not this one: the s099 fix was an OPEN WORK block listing every incident awaiting action, deadline first, with its next_action and drill command - not a hardcoded line about Egypt.
4. No silent caps. The first version capped the list at 8 of 9 live incidents and left INC-FXREVAL-OB09 unreachable; the check caught it on its first run.
5. It is MECHANIZED, not a habit: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/knowledge_reachability_check.py runs in the gate tier of every rebuild and fails when an open incident is not reachable, or when one with a deadline has no next_action.
rules.rule: Storing knowledge is not the same as making it recoverable. Knowledge is LANDED only when it is reachable from the files a fresh session actually reads first - brain_v2/BRAIN_INDEX.md and MEMORY.md - not merely when a store was written.
rules.why: Session #099 landed a complete Purpose of Payment analysis (claims 484-496, two companions, source doc, closed research, first-class incident record) and then measured the entry points: BRAIN_INDEX.md had ZERO mentions of PPC, Egypt or T015L, and so did MEMORY.md, while graph_queries.py incident INC-EGYPT-PPC returned the complete ten-code fix and transport order. The knowledge was durable, queryable and UNREACHABLE: the only way to find it was to already know the incident id, which is exactly what a new session does not know. The index printed '14 incidents' as a COUNT. A count is not a pointer. CP-001: losing traceability is irreversible.

rules.how_to_apply:
1. The scope answer comes first: this project READS SAP, extracts to the golden, analyses the extracted corpus, and builds the brain. It does not write.
2. A kill-switch is not an architecture. ALLOW_D01_WRITES blocks 3 scripts; 88 were never behind it. Do not treat 'the switch is off' as safety.
3. Do NOT connect the MCP server to get a nicer surface - it never ran, and it would bring adt_deploy (no gates) and brain_search (a different brain source).
4. Do not delete them either. Deleting code is not governing it, and two of those scripts are the record of how INC-CLASS-LOSS was recovered. They are inventoried in brain_v2/sap_write_tool_inventory.json and reported every run by capability_ownership_check.py.
5. If a write genuinely has to happen, it happens in the project that owns that capability, through a RELEASED transport, with 4-eyes - never from here.
rules.rule: NEVER invoke a SAP write script from this project. Deploying ABAP is OUT OF SCOPE here. Before running ANY script whose name contains deploy/write/reconstruct/insert/install, check brain_v2/capability_ownership.json - if the capability has no owner, the answer is not 'pick the least bad script', it is 'this does not happen here'.
rules.why: MEASURED s099: 91 scripts in this repo can write to SAP and only 3 have the ALLOW_D01_WRITES kill-switch. The other 88 carry 148 write calls behind no gate, and 68 of them sit in Zagentexecution/mcp-backend-server-python/. They are unused and unreferenced, which IS the danger: a future session finds one and runs it believing it is how we deploy. This is exactly the class of tool that caused INC-CLASS-LOSS (2026-06-12) - writing in place, no transport, no review, on N_MENARD objects we do not own.

rules.how_to_apply:
1. Name the single fact that would decide the question. If one file read or one grep produces it, do that first.
2. Reserve fan-out for work that is genuinely wide: many files, many independent angles, no single decisive fact.
3. Consider the machine. A rebuild had just finished; the box was already loaded. Cost is not only tokens.
4. A background job that dies leaves NOTHING. Prefer a sequence of cheap steps whose partial results survive.
rules.rule: Do not reach for multi-agent orchestration to answer a question a single read can answer. Before launching a workflow, ask: what is the cheapest thing that would settle this? If the answer is 'a grep', run the grep.
rules.why: s099: I launched a 5-lens workflow with per-finding refuters to decide whether a 200-line module should exist. It consumed the user's machine to 100%, returned NOTHING (it died with no completion record and no partial results), and cost about two hours. The question it was meant to settle — does a golden-DB helper already exist? — was answered afterwards in three seconds by one grep that found `import golden_hub as _gh` on line 548. Heavy machinery is not thoroughness; it is a bet, and a bet that returns nothing is worse than a cheap answer that returns something.

rules.how_to_apply:
1. `grep -n '^import\|^from' <file>` before deprecating anything — what a module depends on tells you whether it is bound to the dead layer.
2. A shared directory is a filing decision, not an architectural boundary.
3. Record the correction where the wrong claim lives, so the next session does not inherit it.
rules.rule: Deprecate a COMPONENT, never a directory. Before declaring anything dead, read what it imports and what imports it.
rules.why: s099: I declared Zagentexecution/mcp-backend-server-python/ deprecated as a whole because sap_mcp_server.py had never run. That directory also holds golden_hub.py and rfc_helpers.py — plain Python modules with no `mcp` dependency that work today and are the authoritative implementations of their capabilities. The server imports golden_hub, not the other way round (line 548). I then spent an hour rebuilding golden_hub from scratch because I had declared it dead without reading it.

rules.how_to_apply: Read what exists; attach `provenance_verified=false` with the reason when the metadata cannot vouch for it. The caller gets the data AND is told how far to trust it. Reserve hard refusal for what genuinely does not exist.
rules.rule: A guarded path must cover the whole surface it guards. If it refuses part of the data, people route around it — and routing around loses the guarantee for EVERYTHING, not just for the refused part. Degrade with a warning instead of refusing.
rules.why: s099, measured: golden_hub's manifest described 308 tables while the golden holds 369 tables and 5 views, so it refused 66 objects — including E070/E07T (transports), T512W (payroll) and bseg_union, which IS this project's documented Golden Query. That is why the session wrote ~15 ad-hoc sqlite3 snippets instead of calling it, and every one of those lost the provenance the guard exists to supply.

rules.how_to_apply: 1) User names a subject -> `python brain_v2/load_domain.py <topic>` (aliases: dmee, ppc, sepa, citi, cgi, f110, bcm, ebs, avc, budget, travel, payroll, transport; or any domain name; `--list` to see them). 2) Read part_01..part_NN IN ORDER -- all of them. 3) Read the PERIPHERAL list; pull by path anything the question actually needs. 4) ONLY THEN reason. If the load is too large for the remaining budget, say so with the measured number and read the CORE docs + companions first -- never silently skip and never claim readiness you do not have. 5) If the topic resolves to no domain, add the alias to ALIASES in load_domain.py rather than grepping ad hoc. MECANIZADA: brain_v2/session_start_hook.py exige el load_domain en cuanto se nombra un tema.
rules.rule: The moment a topic or domain is named, run `python brain_v2/load_domain.py <topic>` and READ EVERY PART IT EMITS, before proposing, diagnosing or answering. The BRAIN_INDEX orients; it does not make you competent. graph_queries drills return fragments, not the domain's body of knowledge.
rules.why: Session #100: asked to work a DMEE bank-file error, the agent read BRAIN_INDEX + a graph_queries search + 230 lines of one doc and declared itself ready. On disk, unread, sat 40 domain docs, 20 companions, 165 claims and 11 incidents -- ~667K tokens of existing, verified knowledge. Tiered bootstrap (s079) solved context rot at BOOTSTRAP and created a hole at WORK: nothing existed between the 4KB index and the 400K brain, so every session re-discovered its own corpus by grepping and the user had to demand the load, every time. Re-discovery is not free: it burns the session, it is incomplete, and it silently re-derives what is already verified (violates CP-001 traceability and CP-003 evidence).

rules.how_to_apply: Cuando exista deadline regulatorio: (1) evaluar contra el texto de la norma, no contra el historico de aceptacion; (2) si la herramienta tiene modo futuro — como pain001_address_validator.py --after-nov2026 — usarlo SIEMPRE, no solo cuando lo pidan; (3) no presentar 'pasa hoy' como tranquilizador sin decir que la regla aun no aplica.
rules.rule: Que hoy lo acepten NO es evidencia de que cumplira cuando la regla entre en vigor. Ante un cambio normativo con fecha, medir SIEMPRE contra la regla publicada, nunca contra el comportamiento observado durante el periodo de gracia.
rules.why: 2026-08-19: reporte 'CITI no lo rechazara' apoyandome en que 11.185 pagos pasaron en 2026. JP lo corto: 'hoy no los rechaza porque no esta en vigencia la direccion estructurada'. Tenia razon: la aceptacion actual era ausencia de control, no conformidad. Con la base correcta, la exposicion del rail CITI son 5.239 pagos (46%) sin CtrySubDvsn contra una regla escrita — pasa de 'apuesta si endurecen' a trabajo con fecha.

rules.how_to_apply: Existe la herramienta: dmee_tree_map.py para formatos de pago. Para otros sistemas, construirla antes de responder la primera pregunta. El mapa se GENERA y lleva fecha de medida; no se escribe a mano, porque un doc de configuracion escrito a mano se desincroniza en la primera edicion y se lee como si fuera cierto. MECANIZADA: brain_v2/session_start_hook.py lo inyecta en cada arranque; Zagentexecution/quality_checks/dmee_tree_map.py es el mapa para formatos de pago.
rules.rule: Ante una pregunta sobre un sistema CONFIGURADO (arboles DMEE, customizing, jerarquias), construir o refrescar su MAPA COMPLETO antes de responder — no solo la parte que la pregunta toca. Una sonda por pregunta re-deriva una foto parcial cada vez y omite EN SILENCIO lo que la pregunta no nombro.
rules.why: 2026-08-19: se entrego una especificacion de cambio del CdtrAgt de CGI leyendo solo el mapping. En ese arbol 392 de 628 nodos (62%) cuelgan de un exit que no se estaba mirando. Se analizaron 3 arboles habiendo 6 formatos vivos. JP tuvo que decirlo dos veces: 'estan los codigos de las extensiones para cada elemento' y 'eso aplica a todos los arboles y eso es lo que mas me preocupa que desconoces'. Cuando por fin se construyo el mapa entero tardo 90 segundos y encontro tres defectos que ninguna sonda habia visto, incluido un orden ISO roto en /SEPA_CT_UNES que llevaba meses latente.

rules.how_to_apply: Antes de lanzar la consulta, escribir los cortes y por que cada uno discrimina. Si no se sabe nombrar el corte, no se entiende la tabla todavia. Ver la cabecera de structured_address_readiness.py, que los lleva escritos con el error que costo cada uno. MECANIZADA: los tres cortes (DORIGIN, T042Z, rail) estan DENTRO de Zagentexecution/quality_checks/structured_address_readiness.py, no en un comentario; y session_start_hook.py los nombra al arrancar.
rules.rule: Toda medida sobre una tabla transaccional declara PRIMERO sus dimensiones discriminantes. Omitir una inventa un problema o esconde otro. En pagos (REGUH) son tres: DORIGIN (quien cobra -- cada origen tiene su fuente de verdad), T042Z (por donde sale -- FORMI=fichero, XSCHK=cheque), y el rail (contra que regla se mide -- los bancos no piden lo mismo).
rules.why: 2026-08-19, el mismo error tres veces en un dia. rules.how_to_apply: test_<herramienta>.py junto a la herramienta, ejecutable sin SAP, cubriendo las funciones puras: claves, clasificaciones, detecciones. MECANIZADA: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/run_all_tests.py corre todos los test_*.py y esta enganchado al hook Stop, asi que se ejecuta al cerrar.
rules.rule: Toda herramienta reutilizable lleva un test que corre SIN conexion, y sus casos son errores REALES ya cometidos, no ejemplos inventados: asi el test documenta la trampa ademas de vigilarla.
rules.why: 2026-08-19: el test de structured_address_readiness.py tardo cinco minutos en escribirse y caza en el acto que el detector de codigos postales comodin anclaba al final y NO reconocia '99999-9999' ni 'Z9Z 9Z9' — 64 de los 68 casos reales. Sin el, habria vuelto a derivar Alaska para una direccion de New York y cargado el dato falso en el maestro. No se vio leyendo el codigo: se vio ejecutandolo.

rules.how_to_apply: Al cerrar sesion, por cada regla nueva elegir una existente y (a) mecanizarla en un check ejecutable, o (b) retirarla si ya no aplica. Preferir siempre mecanizar sobre escribir. MECANIZADA: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/rules_mechanization_check.py mide el % del corpus con algo ejecutable detras y nombra las CRITICAL huerfanas. Enganchado al hook Stop. Linea base 2026-08-19: 14 de 213 (6%).
rules.rule: Por cada regla nueva que se anada al brain, convertir una vieja en comprobacion EJECUTABLE o retirarla. Una regla que exige recordarla no es un mecanismo: es una nota.
