Al mejorar una, pregunta antes: ¿lo que voy a escribir seria una entrega/lectura/llamada REAL si alguien la siguiera? Si la respuesta es 'no, pero cuenta', no lo escribas.
rules.rule: LAS TRES ARISTAS CON LAS QUE MEDIMOS SI NUESTRO CONOCIMIENTO SE APLICA CUENTAN UN PROXY, NO EL HECHO, Y LAS TRES TIENEN EL MISMO TECHO: `LEE` cuenta que el NOMBRE del skill aparezca en el texto -- una CITA, no una lectura. `USA` cuenta un IMPORT -- importar y no llamar puntua igual que usarlo bien. `DELEGA` contaba que un agente NOMBRE a otro -- y medido en s107, 4 de 26 eran menciones de estilo, no entregas. Ninguna de las tres se puede llevar al 100% honestamente pegando texto, pero las tres se PUEDEN llevar al 100% pegando texto, y por eso ninguna vale como objetivo.
rules.why: Un proxy sirve para RANQUEAR donde mirar y no para certificar que algo se aplica. Confundirlos convierte una mejora real en un ejercicio de pegar nombres, y el proyecto ya tiene el caso: el termometro de conectividad subio de 19,7% a 48,8% sin que se conectara nada -- subio porque el DENOMINADOR estaba inflado (claim 622). El riesgo simetrico es inflar el NUMERADOR.

rules.how_to_apply: Antes de disenar cualquier instrumento sobre agentes, skills, subagentes, memoria o contexto: (1) leer `code.claude.com/docs` de la pieza concreta -- puede que el mecanismo YA EXISTA y no haya que construir nada; (2) leer `anthropic.com/engineering` del tema, que trae las cifras con las que juzgar si merece la pena; (3) solo entonces papers. Registrar la version del harness observada: sus capacidades tienen fecha (`skills:` y el roster de hermanos no existian siempre). Y si anthropic.com no responde -- paso hoy, ECONNREFUSED en dos intentos -- decirlo y marcar la cifra como transcrita de tercero, NUNCA darla por leida en la fuente.
rules.rule: ANTE CUALQUIER PREGUNTA SOBRE COMO CONSTRUIR, MEDIR U OPERAR AGENTES, ANTHROPIC ES FUENTE OBLIGATORIA -- no una mas. Instruccion del dueno, s107: «siempre usa Anthropic como fuente, es un must; siempre evoluciona sus herramientas». Y no es preferencia de marca: es que el harness sobre el que corremos ES suyo, asi que su documentacion no describe una practica recomendable, describe LO QUE NUESTRAS PROPIAS HERRAMIENTAS HACEN -- y cambia sin que nadie nos avise. Dos sitios, los dos: (1) anthropic.com/engineering (como miden lo que construyen) y (2) code.claude.com/docs (el contrato exacto del harness). Lo academico se lee DESPUES y para el metodo, no para el mecanismo.
rules.why: Medido el mismo dia que se escribio esta regla. La lectura academica (MAST, arXiv:2503.13657) dijo 'mide sobre trazas' y dejo abierto QUE medir. La fuente de Anthropic lo cerro con numeros: el uso de tokens explica el 80% de la varianza de rendimiento y con llamadas a herramientas y modelo el 95%; el coste es ~15x el de un chat; ~20 consultas bastan para detectar cambios; un LLM-juez UNICO con rubrica bate a varios especializados; y la causa numero uno de mala delegacion es la DESCRIPCION DE TAREA VAGA. Y la documentacion del harness destapo DOS MECANISMOS QUE TENIAMOS Y NO USABAMOS: el campo `skills:` del front-matter PRECARGA el contenido completo de un skill en el contexto del subagente -- que convierte 'lee esto primero' de consejo en mecanismo -- y desde v2.1.206 el harness pasa un ROSTER DE HERMANOS, que es exactamente el fallo de coordinacion que Anthropic documenta. Sin esas dos lecturas habriamos escrito otra metrica declarativa y seguido ignorando el consejo del coordinador, que es el fallo que costo tres errores publicados en el circuito P2P ese mismo dia.

rules.how_to_apply: Antes de concluir que algo 'no se usa', contesta primero: ¿SE PUEDE llegar? ¿Esta en el directorio que la herramienta escanea? ¿Aparece en algun listado que se cargue solo? ¿Su uso es el comportamiento POR DEFECTO o hay que optar por el? Si contestar cuesta escribir codigo, nadie contestara -- haz que lo barato sea lo correcto. Y al crear un instrumento, declara EN EL MISMO ACTO por donde se llega a el: un artefacto sin via de acceso nace muerto. Contraste util: si el arreglo es 'recordar', es el arreglo equivocado.
rules.rule: UN INSTRUMENTO AL QUE NADIE PUEDE LLEGAR ES DOCUMENTACION, POR MUY BIEN ESCRITO QUE ESTE -- Y LA ALCANZABILIDAD ES ESTRUCTURAL, NO CUESTION DE DISCIPLINA. Medido en s107 en TRES capas del mismo dia. (1) LAS 50 SKILLS DE SAP vivian en `.agents/skills/`, un directorio que el harness NO ESCANEA: ninguna era invocable, 106 KB de metodo de banca que el modelo no podia cargar. La metrica que publicabamos -- '24 skills sin ningun lector' -- NO medía desidia: medía imposibilidad. (2) LOS 72 MINEROS: los 72 con script que existe, y 49 (68%) sin nadie que los invoque, porque solo corrian si alguien recordaba abrir `algorithms.json`, un JSON de 96 fichas que ninguna sesion carga. (3) EL FORO DE MINERIA: 49 mineros PUBLICAN y UNO SOLO podia contestar, porque contestar exigia que cada minero implementase su propia funcion. 47 preguntas, 14 respuestas: no era un foro, era un megafono.
rules.why: Las tres veces la conclusion facil habria sido 'los consumidores no se acuerdan' -- y las tres veces era FALSA: no se podia llegar. Diagnosticar como falta de disciplina lo que es un defecto de estructura lleva a escribir recordatorios, que es lo unico que seguro no funciona. Y el coste es doble: se pierde el conocimiento Y se acusa al consumidor. La prueba de que era estructura y no costumbre: al mover las skills al directorio correcto pasaron a estar disponibles EN LA MISMA SESION, sin que nadie cambiara de habito.

rules.how_to_apply: Al registrar CUALQUIER entrada nueva en un store estructurado: (1) identifica la clave EXACTA que la puerta que lo gatea lee -- grep el nombre de la clave en el SCRIPT del check (`.get("algorithms"`, `.get("rules"`, etc.), no en el JSON: son preguntas distintas; (2) escribe DENTRO de esa clave, nunca en la raiz del fichero ni en una clave hermana marcada con `_`; (3) antes de elegir un prefijo/id, busca si YA EXISTE dentro del registro -- una colision de nombre entre dos taxonomias es tan grave como estar fuera de el; (4) tras registrar, CORRE el gate y confirma que el conteo que reporta subio EXACTAMENTE en el numero de entradas anadidas -- un PASS cuyo denominador no cambio es la senal de este defecto, no una confirmacion de que todo esta bien.
rules.rule: UN VERDE DE UNA PUERTA SOLO VALE SOBRE LA POBLACION QUE LA PUERTA RECORRE -- si algo se registra FUERA del contenedor que la puerta lee, la puerta da PASS sin haberlo mirado nunca, y un verde por no mirar es peor que un rojo. Medido en s108/s109: D1-D6 (y luego D7, heredado por otro agente) se registraron en la RAIZ de brain_v2/methods/algorithms.json, fuera de la clave `algorithms` donde viven las entradas reales que algorithm_landing_check.py recorre (`container = raw.get("algorithms", raw)`). Ademas los prefijos D1/D4/D5/D6 YA EXISTIAN dentro con otro significado (D1_D3_delta_strategies, D4_field_splitting, D5_bounded_probe_with_cap_reporting, D6_aggregate_before_resolve) -- dos taxonomias distintas con el mismo nombre en el mismo store, invisibles la una a la otra. Migrados a A72-A78 DENTRO del registro (Zagentexecution/tasks/2026_08_28_ebs_ntb02_uno18eur/migrate_miner_registry.py); el registro paso de 98 a 105 entradas y las cifras dependientes se movieron al hacerse visibles (mineros del braintoolbox 72->74, gates 62->70).
rules.why: Un gate que RECORRE una coleccion (`for k in container`) no comprueba que la coleccion este COMPLETA -- comprueba solo lo que encuentra dentro de ella. Escribir al nivel equivocado del mismo fichero JSON no rompe el parseo (sigue siendo JSON valido) ni hace fallar al gate (que sigue devolviendo PASS, honestamente, sobre lo que SI vio): produce silencio estructural, indistinguible de que todo esta bien. Es un paso mas atras que 'creerse el propio print' (verificar por lo que se emite y no por lo que se guarda): aqui ni siquiera hay una emision equivocada, hay un CONTENEDOR equivocado, y por eso ninguna lectura del propio hallazgo lo habria detectado -- solo mirar el fichero completo y comparar contra lo que el gate declara leer. La colision de prefijo (D1 fuera == D1 dentro con otro significado) agrava el defecto: aunque alguien abriera el JSON entero, el nombre compartido sugiere que es LO MISMO cuando son dos taxonomias independientes.

rules.how_to_apply: Antes de publicar cualquier hallazgo con un CONTEO o una SUMA (pagos, cuentas, USD, pares, filas): (1) comprueba que el mismo objeto que agrega TAMBIEN serializa la lista de sujetos que componen el agregado -- si el agregado es N y la lista trae menos de N o esta vacia, hay una fuga; (2) CORRE el instrumento y lee el FICHERO DE SALIDA, no el codigo -- un bloque muerto tras un `return` parsea perfecto y no se detecta leyendo el codigo con calma, solo corriendolo y comprobando el EFECTO (regla #180 `feedback_a_silent_replace_is_a_silent_defect`, ya existente: enlaza esta comprobacion a ella, no la dupliques); (3) adjunta la lista de sujetos al hallazgo DEL BUS, no solo al fichero de tarea de turno -- un JSON de tarea que nadie vuelve a abrir es tan invisible como el bloque muerto que lo alimentaba.
rules.rule: UN HALLAZGO PUBLICADO CON UN AGREGADO Y SIN SUJETOS IDENTIFICABLES NO ES ACCIONABLE -- el instrumento tiene que SERIALIZAR los sujetos (cuenta, persona, documento), no solo contarlos. Medido en s109: `bank_statement_sod_check.py` calculaba el ciclo completo de 4 eslabones (crea la factura + emite el pago + teclea el extracto que lo confirma) y publico al bus 'hallazgo 59' como '60 pagos, 65.409,13 USD, 9 pares' -- pero el bloque que imprimia y guardaba esos nueve pares (cuenta, persona) vivia DESPUES del `return` de `informe()`: codigo inalcanzable, nunca corrio. Auditoria/Tesoreria no puede revisar '9 pares'; solo puede revisar 9 pares CON NOMBRE. Corregido moviendo el bloque antes del return, serializandolo en sod_bank_statement.json y adjuntando la lista (campo `pares`) al hallazgo 59 del bus -- ese mismo movimiento saco a la luz una asimetria que nadie habria adivinado del agregado solo (los pares de 4 eslabones no son subconjunto de los de 3).
rules.why: Es la version silenciosa de 'creerse el propio print' (feedback_a_silent_replace_is_a_silent_defect, #180): aqui ni siquiera habia un print equivocado, habia un print que NUNCA se ejecutaba, y el agregado que SI se publico (60/65.409/9) parecia completo por si solo -- daba la falsa sensacion de que el hallazgo ya era accionable cuando en realidad trasladaba el trabajo de identificar los sujetos a quien lo leyera despues, sin darle ni los datos ni el contexto para reconstruirlos. Un conteo correcto con contenido perdido es mas peligroso que un conteo que falla ruidosamente: el primero se cierra como 'hecho' sin haber servido para nada.

rules.how_to_apply: 1) Cuando una sonda/gate marca NO/FALTA sobre algo que sabes que existe, para ANTES de tocar el dato: la pregunta es '¿por que la sonda no lo ve?', no '¿como hago que la sonda lo vea?'. 2) Lee el codigo de la sonda: identifica EXACTAMENTE que campo lee y compara contra el campo real del dato (canonical_key vs registry_keys, alias vs canonico, clave de store vs clave de negocio). 3) Si el dato es mas preciso o mas correcto que lo que la sonda espera, la sonda es el defecto -- arreglala para leer el campo correcto (con fallback), nunca degrades el dato a lo que la sonda sabe leer. 4) Tras arreglar la sonda, vuelve a correrla sobre el caso original SIN tocar el dato y confirma verde -- si necesitas tocar el dato para que pase, no arreglaste la sonda, la esquivaste. 5) Registra la correccion como correccion MIA en el commit/retro, no como 'dato corregido' -- la trazabilidad de que casi se acomodo el mundo a una puerta rota es parte de la evidencia (CP-001).
rules.rule: SI UNA PUERTA Y UN DATO DISCREPAN, LA PRIMERA SOSPECHA ES LA PUERTA, NUNCA EL DATO -- editar el dato para que la puerta se ponga en verde es al reves. Medido en s108/s109: work_triad_check.py daba NO en proceso y NO en metodo para INC-000013624. El domain declarado era 'Treasury_EBS' y se cambio a 'Treasury' para que la sonda encontrara registro -- pero Treasury_EBS ERA correcto: es canonical_key de la ontologia con registry_keys=['Treasury'], y la sonda resolvia por canonical_key crudo sin leer ese campo, asi que daba registro VACIO para cualquier dominio cuya clave de registro no coincidiera con su nombre canonico. Restaurado el dato (Treasury_EBS) y arreglada la sonda (lee domains[].registry_keys como fallback).
rules.why: El resultado se ve IDENTICO en los dos casos -- verde -- y por eso el atajo es tentador: cambiar el dato es una linea, arreglar la sonda exige entender por que falla. Pero editar el dato deja DOS danos, no uno: (1) el dato queda peor de lo que estaba (Treasury_EBS es mas preciso que Treasury -- distingue el dominio EBS de Treasury en general, y esa distincion existe por algo, tiene su propia fila en la ontologia); (2) la puerta sigue ciega para el SIGUIENTE incidente cuyo canonical_key no coincida con su registry_key -- el defecto no se cierra, se esconde detras de un caso que ya no lo dispara. Es la misma familia que feedback_gate_coverage_is_bounded_by_what_it_walks: una puerta que no ve toda su poblacion miente con un verde honesto, y aqui alguien acomodo el mundo (el dato) a la mentira de la puerta en vez de agrandar lo que la puerta ve. Y la correccion casi la cometio la MISMA persona que un dia antes habia escrito la regla sobre denominadores incompletos -- interiorizar una regla en la sesion en que se escribe no evita repetir su modo de fallo al dia siguiente, sobre otro objeto.

_definition.profile: The measured reality of ONE tenant/system landscape: what is installed, what is configured, what is productive, how it is operated, who uses it, and through which channels data enters and leaves.

_evidence_tiers.CONFIGURED: organisational structure / customising exists (company code, sales org, plant, asset company code...).
_evidence_tiers.INSTALLED: component present in CVERS. Near-meaningless on its own: 177 components are installed and most ship by default.
_evidence_tiers.NOT_EVIDENCED: we have no evidence either way. NOT the same as NOT_USED. Never collapse the two.
_evidence_tiers.NOT_USED: the module exists but zero documents and zero executions — an ASSERTED negative, only valid when actually probed.
_evidence_tiers.PRODUCTIVE: business documents exist AND/OR transactions are executed in the audit log.
_evidence_tiers._adoption_is_a_separate_axis: Do NOT widen this vocabulary to express extent. The TIER answers 'how do we know?'; the optional `adoption` field (FULL/PARTIAL/MARGINAL) answers 'how far is it rolled out?'. Collapsing the two is what produced statuses like 'PARTIAL' that mean neither. Caught by the I1 gate on its first run — the gate paid for itself immediately.
_evidence_tiers._rule: Every module MUST carry one of these. Never state a module without its tier — 'implemented' alone is the ambiguity that caused the s097 failure.

_interrelations._design: The profile is not a leaf. It is the SPINE that the other stores hang off. Each link below is a LOOKUP (explicit key), never a fuzzy token match — the mistake ontology.json already had to correct once.
_interrelations.profile -> capability_model: COMPLEMENTARY, NOT NESTED. Profile = the system. Capability model = our knowledge of it. Do not merge them; the delta between the two IS the backlog.
_interrelations.profile.module -> capability_model.domai: via the above. Answers: for a module that is PRODUCTIVE, do we actually have capability coverage? A PRODUCTIVE module with no capability row is a SYSTEM-LEVEL BLIND SPOT — a different and more serious animal than the object-level blind_spots (L12), which are names we mentioned without a node.
_interrelations.profile.module -> claims: by domain + by related_objects. Every profile assertion must be traceable to a claim with evidence.
_interrelations.profile.module -> knowledge/domains/<x>/: the prose layer (artifact hierarchy: brain .md -> companion .html -> Word).
_interrelations.profile.module -> ontology.canonical_key: explicit `capability_domain` field per module. Resolves the technical module onto the canonical domain vocabulary.
_interrelations.profile.operating_model -> knowledge/sys: the profile SUMMARISES; those docs stay the source of truth for per-flow detail. Never duplicate them here.
_interrelations.profile.third_party_addons -> F_INTERFAC: each add-on is an independent data-exit channel and therefore a governance object, not a licence line item.

_invariants.I1: Every module carries an evidence tier AND its evidence string. No tier without evidence.
_invariants.I2: NOT_USED requires an actual probe. Absence in the Gold DB or in executed_objects_domain_map is a FLOOR, never an inventory — it yields NOT_EVIDENCED, never NOT_USED.
_invariants.I3: Technical component names are resolved from the system (TADIR -> TDEVC -> DF14L), never from memory.
_invariants.I4: The profile is rendered into BRAIN_INDEX.md at bootstrap. If a session has to re-derive the footprint, the profile has failed — fix the profile, do not answer from scratch.
_invariants.I5: The profile is TENANT-SCOPED. Nothing here is portable to another client; the CONCEPT and the build scripts are.

_maintenance._superseded: s097. This field previously read 'any session that measures something — EDIT unesco_system_profile.json'. That made the profile unreproducible on a second installation, which is the one thing the profile exists for.
_maintenance.gate: build_profile_links.py still FAILS LOUD on an invariant breach. P1 does not replace it — P1 says WHERE each part of the profile comes from, the links gate says whether the parts are consistent.
_maintenance.how: run the analysis cycle; P1 composes at the end. A component reported MISSING names the algorithm to run. A component reported DECLARED is hand work that a human still owes and that must be redone on the next tenant.
_maintenance.who_updates: NOTHING edits the profile by hand any more. It is COMPOSED from 18 components by brain_v2/system_profile/compose_profile.py (algorithm P1), each component bound to the algorithm that derives it.

_module_to_domain._authority: EXPLICIT mapping, hand-maintained. `null` = no canonical domain exists yet -> that is a finding, not an error. s097: PBC/FI_AA/PM/SD/TRM/CO mapped to new same-named capability rows after the crossing exposed them as system-level blind spots.

_concept._one_line: The PROFILE is what the TENANT IS. The capability model is what WE KNOW about it. Two different questions about the same system — and the delta between them is the work.

_strata.1_footprint: installed / configured / productive per module + org structure. Cheap, factual, and the thing external parties always ask for first.
_strata.2_operation: HOW it is run: channel mix (dialog vs RFC vs IDoc vs batch vs file), who orchestrates, read vs write direction. This is where UNESCO's 80.6%-external headline lives.
_strata.3_periphery: what surrounds the core: third-party add-ons, the digital front-end (OData/Fiori), users and licences, and every channel through which data EXITS. Systematically forgotten, and the richest for a governance conversation.
_strata.note: The profile has three strata, in increasing order of what they cost to establish and of what they are worth.

_why_a_new_concept.diagnosis: Those 6 were not unknown — they were UNADDRESSED. PBC was in the brain as an 'engine' inside a prose doc; RE-FX had a domain folder; the add-ons had a companion. Knowledge existed but was not KEYED on the question being asked. A store you cannot query by the question you are asked is not knowledge, it is storage.
_why_a_new_concept.principle: CP-001 traceability + CP-003 evidence. A concept earns its place when a whole CLASS of question has no home. 'What is this tenant?' is that class.
_why_a_new_concept.trigger: s097 — an external Business Process Review asked 'which modules are implemented and which are actively used'. The brain could not answer it. It held the HOW (operating model: 80.6% external orchestration; 37 integration flows) and it held OUR KNOWLEDGE (capability_model: domain x 11 capabilities), but nowhere did it hold the WHAT: the tenant's own footprint. The answer had to be re-derived live from cvers + audit logs and was wrong on 6 modules (RE-FX, SD, FI-AA, PM, TRM, PBC) plus an entire missing category (third-party add-ons).

system_profile._design: THE UNESCO PROFILE — the base fact-sheet of the tenant: what SAP is installed, what is really implemented, what actually runs, and HOW it is operated. This is the FIRST thing a session (or an external reviewer) needs; the capability_model (L15) then says how well we KNOW each domain. Profile = the system; capability_model = our knowledge of it. Do not merge them, do not duplicate them.

_evidence_tiers.CONFIGURED: organisational structure / customising exists (company code, sales org, plant, asset cocd...).
_evidence_tiers.INSTALLED: component present in CVERS. Says nothing about use — most ECC components ship by default.
_evidence_tiers.PRODUCTIVE: business documents exist AND/OR the transactions are executed in the audit log.

_links._what_this_is: The PROFILE crossed against capability_model / ontology / claims / knowledge docs / companions. Read `system_level_blind_spots` first.

capability_domains_without_a_profile_mod._meaning: The mirror gap: domains we model but never tied to a real module — either cross-cutting (Integration, Closing) or a modelling artefact to reconcile.

system_level_blind_spots._meaning: Modules the tenant runs IN PRODUCTION that have NO row in the capability model — i.e. our operating model has never looked at them. Distinct from L12 blind_spots (names without a graph node). These are the expensive ones.

_anti_methods.A1_absence_in_a_derived_index: Absence in executed_objects_domain_map or in the Gold DB is a FLOOR, never an inventory. It yields NOT_EVIDENCED, never NOT_USED. Cost: 5 modules wrongly reported as not implemented.
_anti_methods.A2_substring_name_matching: Matching a module name as a substring of free text. 'CO' matched 337 claims, 'PM' 47, 'SD' 30 — noise presented as coverage, which is worse than an empty list because it reads as linkage.
_anti_methods.A3_suppressing_a_generic_error: TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA was being swallowed as 'empty is normal'. It was masking an INVALID FIELD (PARENT_ID on DF14L), and three extraction runs returned 0 rows with no error. Never suppress a generic error class without first confirming what it is hiding.
_anti_methods.A4_answering_from_memory: SAP component codes, table names and field names must be resolved from the system. Every code in the profile came from DF14L, not recall.
_anti_methods._note: Activities that LOOK like evidence and are not. Each cost real errors in s097.

_maturity_methods._concept: MODEL MATURITY METHODS — the repeatable activities that mature the model

_cycle._why: Maturity is the LOOP, not the run. Logs accumulate -> operating model sharpens -> domains resolve -> profile updates -> coherence re-checks -> gaps move. Cadences are declared in the SKILL.
_cycle.daily: accumulate_logs.py — the only activity whose value is DESTROYED BY DELAY (source purges in 7-120 days)
_cycle.quarterly: probe_footprint.py + extract_component_hierarchy.py — the FOOTPRINT DRIFTS and nothing detects it automatically

_lifecycle.1_discovered: an activity performed by hand in a conversation, once
_lifecycle.2_scripted: written as a runnable tool with its inputs and outputs declared
_lifecycle.3_wired: runs inside rebuild_all.py — it can no longer be forgotten
_lifecycle.4_gated: FAILS the rebuild when its invariant is breached — it can no longer be ignored
_lifecycle.5_measured: its output feeds a maturity metric, so we can see the model getting better
_lifecycle._rule: An activity below stage 3 is not part of the product yet. Promote it or drop it — do not leave it at stage 1 as a note.

_next_promotions.P1: Schedule M1 (footprint probe) to re-run periodically — the footprint DRIFTS as the tenant changes, and nothing currently detects that.
_next_promotions.P2: Raise M4 ascent above 64.5% by extending TADIR coverage past the 40,000-row cap per object type (P01 rejects ROWSKIPS, so chunk by name range instead).
_next_promotions.P3: Feed M5 coherence into meta_capability.py so model drift becomes a MEASURED maturity lever rather than a report nobody reads.
_next_promotions.P4: Re-run the extended classifier (process_mining/executed_objects_domain_map.py) to shrink the 40%-of-volume 'Uncatalogued' bucket now that RE-FX, PBC, FI-AA, PM, SD, TRM and the add-on namespaces have rules.
_next_promotions._note: Activities still at stage 1-2. Each is a known lever, not a vague idea.

_maturity_methods._one_line: Results are the output; METHODS are the product. A discovery that stays in a conversation dies with the session. A discovery turned into a runnable, scheduled check compounds.

_why.principle: The model is not the set of facts it holds. It is the set of activities it can repeat. Facts age; activities compound.
_why.test: For anything learned this session ask: what ACTIVITY found it, is that activity runnable, and does it run on its own? If the answer to any of those is no, the learning is not yet part of the product.
_why.trigger: s097 discovered six productive modules the model had never seen, a whole category of third-party add-ons, and an entire missing brain concept (the PROFILE). Every one of those was found by an ACTIVITY, not by luck: a bounded probe, a crossing, a gate. If only the findings are recorded, the next blind spot waits for another accident.

M10_capability_reevaluation.activity: Walk the capability catalogue and move at least one STATE upward.
M10_capability_reevaluation.answers: Which capability is weakest, and what is the specific lever?
M10_capability_reevaluation.current_portfolio: STRONG 11 · WORKS 12 · WEAK 4 · FRAGILE 1 (accumulate_logs: most valuable, least protected)
M10_capability_reevaluation.why: Capabilities that are never re-evaluated never improve. A catalogue entry whose Improve line has not changed in five sessions is either finished or abandoned — decide which.

M11_trigger_evaluation.activity: Evaluate accumulation / maturity / interpretation triggers against the model's current state.
M11_trigger_evaluation.answers: What needs re-running RIGHT NOW, and why?

families.ACCUMULATION: enough new evidence arrived that an answer may have changed
families.INTERPRETATION: new logs or interfaces can CHANGE THE MEANING of a domain, not just add to it
families.MATURITY: a score moved the wrong way — the model detecting its own regression

M11_trigger_evaluation.principle: A domain assignment is a HYPOTHESIS carried with its evidence window. Extend the window materially and it is due for re-derivation.

M12_investment_alignment.activity: Measure whether capability sits where the work is, and whether the DIFFERENTIATOR tier is our strongest.
M12_investment_alignment.answers: Is the portfolio aligned with the product thesis?
M12_investment_alignment.found_in_s097: MISALLOCATED — PS, PBC and Cost_Recovery_CRP are differentiator-tier and under-modelled, while PS carries 402,845 executions per asset.

M13_path_integrity.fires: rebuild_all step 0a3 + the analysis cycle + per close
M13_path_integrity.promotion: born s097 from a defect found twice in one hour, in two different stores. Promoted from correction to gate on the second sighting — the rule this project keeps re-learning is that a defect appearing twice is structural.
M13_path_integrity.question: does every field that claims to hold a path actually hold one?
M13_path_integrity.why: a path field holding prose makes every check over it silently wrong — not loudly broken, WRONG. C3 was reported as an unimplemented idea while its tool was on disk and running. The catalogue lying about itself is worse than a gap, because a gap is visible.

M14_write_path_discovery.fires: per domain when a table has no known maintenance transaction; on any new object class appearing in the change log; before writing a domain doc
M14_write_path_discovery.promotion: born s097 from the PBC analysis. Generalised on the spot because the same join answers it for every domain — the analysis was never the point.
M14_write_path_discovery.question: for anything that changes, WHAT writes it and through which channel?
M14_write_path_discovery.why: a domain whose tables have no maintenance transaction is not understood — it is merely listed. The write path is the behaviour. And an empty transaction code is not an absence: it usually means a BAPI or RFC whose design never set one, which makes it a POINTER to the interface layer rather than a dead end.

M15_agent_freshness.fires: the analysis cycle + per close + after any claim supersedes a data source
M15_agent_freshness.promotion: born s097 the moment a superseded table was found inside two skills. Written as a check rather than a correction, per rule #172.
M15_agent_freshness.question: do the agents still know what the model knows?
M15_agent_freshness.why: an agent is FROZEN KNOWLEDGE — written on one day against one understanding, with nothing to tell it when that understanding moves. The cost is not theoretical: the CHANGE-AUDIT skill was reading a scope-filtered copy of the change log, the one table its entire purpose depends on, and the FI domain agent still said cdhdr 'needs extraction' with 12M rows on disk. An agent answering confidently from a superseded fact is worse than one that says nothing, because it is trusted.

M16_prose_to_structure.fires: the analysis cycle + whenever an analysis produces a classification
M16_prose_to_structure.promotion: born s097 when the user pointed out the interface channels had been analysed and left unclassified. Cleared one immediately (build_channel_registry.py) and made the rest a measured worklist.
M16_prose_to_structure.question: which analysis exists only as prose, where no algorithm can reach it?
M16_prose_to_structure.why: a classification only a human can read gets RE-DERIVED by the next question, and the two answers drift with nothing able to notice. The integration map classified 48 flows into 8 channels; interface_boundary.json contained the word 'channel' zero times, and a new algorithm was about to re-derive the whole taxonomy blind.

M1_footprint_probe.activity: Bounded read-only probe of the tenant's module footprint (org structure + document volumes per module).
M1_footprint_probe.answers: Which modules are CONFIGURED and which are PRODUCTIVE — as opposed to merely installed.
M1_footprint_probe.cost: ~2 minutes, read-only, no writes to SAP
M1_footprint_probe.fires: on demand + whenever a scope question arrives that the profile cannot answer
M1_footprint_probe.found_in_s097: FI-AA, SD, PM, TRM and RE-FX are all PRODUCTIVE — all five had been reported as 'not implemented / not evidenced'.
M1_footprint_probe.invariant: bounded: WHERE year >= 2024 and a ROWCOUNT cap. A hit cap is reported as '>=cap', NEVER as an exact count.

M2_component_resolution.activity: Resolve any SAP object to its APPLICATION COMPONENT via the system's own taxonomy: TADIR -> TDEVC -> DF14L.
M2_component_resolution.answers: What does this object belong to? — the deterministic bottom-up rung.
M2_component_resolution.fires: when the component hierarchy is stale or a new object type is needed
M2_component_resolution.found_in_s097: PBC = PA-PM-PB, which sits under Personnel Management and not under PSM. That single fact explains why an FM-shaped search never found the largest staff-budget capability in the tenant.
M2_component_resolution.invariant: never infer a component from a name when the chain can resolve it
M2_component_resolution.why_it_beats_the_alternative: Package-name regex is guessing. DF14L is SAP stating the answer. Coverage of graph objects rose from 4% to 100% of resolvable objects once the chain spanned object TYPES, not just programs.
M2_component_resolution.writes_to: Gold DB tables df14l (2,687 components) + tadir_obj (311K objects across 10 types)

M3_profile_crossing.activity: Cross the PROFILE against capability model / ontology / claims / docs / companions.
M3_profile_crossing.answers: For every module the tenant RUNS, do we actually model it?
M3_profile_crossing.caught_immediately: two ill-formed statuses (PARTIAL/MARGINAL) that were conflating evidence with adoption
M3_profile_crossing.found_in_s097: 6 blind spots on first run — CO, FI_AA, PM, SD, TRM, PBC — reproducing, from structure alone, exactly the six modules the conversation had got wrong.
M3_profile_crossing.gates: I1 tier+evidence per module · I2 NOT_USED requires a probe · mapping completeness
M3_profile_crossing.produces: SYSTEM-LEVEL BLIND SPOTS = productive module with no capability row

M4_bidirectional_ascent.activity: Climb from every object up to the installation, recording WHICH rung of the evidence ladder resolved it.
M4_bidirectional_ascent.answers: Can we understand the macro profile THROUGH the details? — the stated objective.
M4_bidirectional_ascent.improves_by: extending TADIR coverage to more object types and closing the unresolved tail
M4_bidirectional_ascent.invariant: the rung is ALWAYS recorded — a curated assignment must never be presented as an inference (CP-003)
M4_bidirectional_ascent.metric: pct of graph objects that resolve upward. s097 baseline: 64.5%.

M5_coherence_check.activity: Compare the macro tier asserted top-down against the evidence found bottom-up, per module.
M5_coherence_check.answers: Is the model believing its own summary?
M5_coherence_check.found_in_s097: flagged MM and Payment_BCM as unsupported — which turned out to be an ALIAS DEFECT in the checker itself, not a modelling gap. A self-check that fails loudly is how you find defects in the checker.

verdicts.OK: the macro survives contact with the detail
verdicts.THIN: productive but almost nothing modelled underneath
verdicts.UNSUPPORTED: asserted PRODUCTIVE with zero objects underneath — an assertion with no detail behind it

M5_coherence_check.why_it_matters: This is the only mechanism that can detect the model drifting away from the system it describes.

M6_cross_cutting_overlay.activity: Classify domains that SPAN modules rather than owning one, and make the enrichment edge explicit.
M6_cross_cutting_overlay.answers: What enriches every module instead of belonging to one?
M6_cross_cutting_overlay.fires: rebuild_all.py step 2d; revisit when a new domain has no module
M6_cross_cutting_overlay.found_in_s097: The 'mirror gap' (domains modelled with no module behind them) was not a defect. Those domains are a different KIND. Declaring the kind turned an anomaly into structure.
M6_cross_cutting_overlay.principle: Before treating an anomaly as an error, ask whether it is a category the model lacks.

M7_vocabulary_gate.activity: Refuse any domain key that does not resolve against the canonical ontology.
M7_vocabulary_gate.found_in_s097: rejected the 6 new domains until they were declared. Vocabulary stays canonical BY CONSTRUCTION, not by anyone remembering.
M7_vocabulary_gate.principle: A rule enforced by a human is a wish. A rule enforced by a gate is a property.

M8_alias_resolution.activity: Resolve any domain/doc/module spelling through the ontology's declared aliases before concluding something is missing.
M8_alias_resolution.fires: continuously — imported by every consumer via brain_v2/canonical.py
M8_alias_resolution.found_in_s097: 4 domain docs reported as MISSING already existed under alias folder names (PSM_FM->PSM, Payment_BCM->Payment, Treasury_EBS->Treasury, MM->Procurement). Writing them would have duplicated existing knowledge (CP-002 breach).
M8_alias_resolution.invariant: never compare domain names raw; always normalise through the ontology first
M8_alias_resolution.recurrence: This same defect appeared THREE times in one session — doc resolution, claim matching, coherence checking. It is the single most repeated failure mode in this codebase.

M9_skill_coverage_audit.activity: Audit the portable skill against the repository's real tool surface.
